conviction_note: Mild negative lean (p_up 46) on a name whose print turns on whether the reiterated $400-420M FY adj. EBITDA guide survives. Holding it needs H2 EBITDA of $222-242M against $130.5M in H2 2025, roughly 10 points of margin expansion year on year, while H2 GMS is guided to low single digits. The two direct peers confirm a flat secondary market in Q3: Ticketmaster secondary GTV was flat and Vivid Seats GOV +1%. Against that, Citi expects a Q3 EBITDA beat on app downloads, the October refinancing removed the 2030 maturity wall, and short interest is moderate at 6.5 days to cover. The aggregator revenue bar ($518-528M) looks stale against BofA's $2.46B Q3 GMS estimate, so the bar is disputed: findings are capped small and p_up is held near 50. abs_move 14 sits at the 13.6% event-implied move and the 13.0% median reaction, nudged up because the FY guide is in play. impact_sum (-0.3) is smaller than the scaled number because the positives and negatives sit on different lines and partly offset.
bar: Disputed. Aggregator Q3 revenue consensus is $527.8M / EPS $0.11 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/STUB/estimates; it notes the estimate was revised down 7.8% in 3 months) and about $517-519M / EPS $0.14-0.15 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/STUB/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet). Both imply +11-13% revenue growth on Q3 2025's $468.1M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1337634/000119312525280227/d35879dex991.htm). Against that, the company guided H2 2026 GMS to low single-digit growth: FY GMS $10.1-10.3B with H1 about $5.26B, so H2 is about $4.84-5.04B against about $4.8B in H2 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001337634/000162828026056250/q22026stubhubearningsrelea.htm). BofA cut its Q3 GMS estimate to $2.46B from $2.69B (https://finimize.com/content/bofa-says-stubhubs-world-cup-pop-could-fade, undated, after the Q2 print). At a 19% take rate that is about $470-490M of revenue, so the aggregator figures probably still hold pre-Q2 estimates. Company guide: FY adj. EBITDA $400-420M reiterated; no Q3 guide. No Q3 adj. EBITDA consensus found. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the aggregator revenue bar.

That is 7.7% of 382M shares outstanding and a larger share of float, since Madrone holds about 76M and Baker about 12M (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/stub/short-interest; Madrone holdings from Form 4 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1337634/000162828026062788/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1789775752.xml). Spot $5.63 is 70.75% below the 52-week high and 6.23% above the low, -7.1% over 5 days and -3.9% over 20 days.

findings.finding: Both direct peers that have reported Q3 2026 show a flat secondary ticket market. Live Nation (2026-11-05): 'Secondary ticket GTV flat, with growth in sports offsetting lower concert resale activity ... consistent with efforts to constrain scalper sales.' Vivid Seats (2026-11-09): Marketplace GOV $624.0M, +1% y/y; revenue $126.9M, -7%; orders -11%. Both fit StubHub's own low single-digit H2 GMS guide, which points to Q3 GMS of about $2.45-2.55B against $2.43B a year ago and revenue around $470-490M, below the $518-528M aggregator consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 (2026-08-12) revenue beat consensus by about 12.6% and the GMS guide was raised, yet the stock fell 10.07% on the EPS/margin miss and the soft H2 GMS guide, so the topline has not paid on its own. Q3 2025 (2025-11-13): a revenue beat with no Q4 guide gave -20.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -7.1% over the 5 sessions that cover both peer prints. If the aggregator revenue bar had been reset to the guide, Chartmill and Benzinga would show Q3 revenue near $480M rather than $518-528M. A headline 'revenue miss' against the stale figure is the part still open. The finding lands inside the company's own guide, which keeps it small.
findings.independence: Vivid Seats Q3 2026 release, a different company and document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001856031/000119312526452579/seat-ex99_1.htm (2026-11-09). BofA's Q3 GMS estimate of $2.46B points the same way: https://finimize.com/content/bofa-says-stubhubs-world-cup-pop-could-fade. These are proxies; StubHub has not given a Q3 number.

findings.finding: The reiterated FY 2026 adj. EBITDA guide of $400-420M needs H2 EBITDA of $222.3-242.3M (H1 was $177.7M), against $130.5M in H2 2025 ($67.5M Q3 plus $63M Q4). That is +70-85% on H2 revenue of only about $920-960M (19% of the guided $4.84-5.04B H2 GMS), a margin of about 24-25% against 14% in H2 2025 and 18% in Q2 2026. Peers show no help from the market, so the guide rests entirely on cost efficiency (S&M at 47% of revenue, -800bp y/y in Q2), and a trim or a 'low end' framing is a live risk on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-05-13): FY guide reiterated with 'on track', +13.7%. Q2 2026: EBITDA guide held but not raised alongside an EPS miss, -10.07%. FY2025 print (2026-03-04), first 2026 guide: -12.39%. The guide line is what this stock has traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Much of this is priced. Citi wrote on 2026-09-18 that recent weakness reflected investor concern that StubHub may miss its EBITDA guidance, and the stock sits near its 52-week low with downside skew bid. What is not resolved is the outcome. A reiteration against a market braced for a cut would squeeze; a cut on a name 70% off its high could still move double digits. The arithmetic here is public, so the edge is small and the band is wide.
findings.independence: BofA's H2 GMS cuts (Q3 $2.46B, Q4 $2.50B) and underperform rating point the same way: https://finimize.com/content/bofa-says-stubhubs-world-cup-pop-could-fade. Citi's note says the high end is reachable, which points the other way (see the next finding). The H2 low-single-digit GMS commentary comes from a call summary: https://www.investing.com/equities/stubhub-inc.

findings.finding: Citi upgraded STUB to Buy on 2026-09-18 (PT cut to $7 from $9), saying it expects Q3 adj. EBITDA to beat current forecasts and FY EBITDA could reach the high end of the $400-420M guide. The call rests on app-download tracking: Q3 downloads estimated at 1.4M against 1.2M in Q2, and about 800K more expected in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The EBITDA line has paid when it held: Q1 2026, 50% EBITDA growth with the guide reiterated, gave +13.7%. A 94% EBITDA increase in Q2 still gave -10.07%, because EPS missed and H2 GMS slowed. This name has sold beats.
findings.why_not_priced: A broker note is public, and the stock rose 4.3% on it, then gave that back and more to $5.63. The download series is a proxy that consensus may not have adopted. If it had, the stock would not sit near the 52-week low with puts bid. App downloads are a weak link to marketplace GMS when industry resale is flat.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary: management expects marketing-efficiency gains to support H2 margins and gross margin to return to the mid-80s after the World Cup (https://www.hstong.com/news/hk/detail/10260814177801754, via search snippet). Same direction, but company commentary from before the quarter.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-14 StubHub amended its credit agreement (Amendment No. 7). It extended the USD and Euro TLB maturities 3.5 years, from March 2030 to October 2033, and cut pricing 25bp (USD at SOFR+450, EUR at EURIBOR+475). The USD TLB rose to $975M (from $804M) and the Euro TLB fell to EUR300M (from EUR452M), with the total unchanged. $425M of the $565M revolver now runs to 2031. The $804M pre-amendment USD balance, against $904.2M at June 30, confirms the $100M July paydown and no further paydown in August-October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 headlined $200M of YTD debt reduction and 3.0x net leverage, and the stock still fell 10%, so deleveraging has not been a driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since October 14 and mostly priced. Asked what the money buys: no new money; it is an extension and repricing, which lenders signing at a tighter spread treat as a vote of credit confidence. That removes refinancing risk from the equity story and lowers interest expense by about $3M a year. Small positive, not distress.
findings.independence: Company press release, same event: https://s204.q4cdn.com/138970181/files/doc_news/StubHub-Announces-Extension-of-Senior-Credit-Facilities-2026.pdf. Shares the document base.

findings.finding: Positioning: 29.5M shares short at 6.48 days to cover (2026-10-15 settlement), 7.7% of shares outstanding and a larger share of float given Madrone's ~76M and Baker's ~12M shares. Front-expiry open interest is call-heavy (put/call OI 0.29) despite +14.6 vol points of put skew. A reiterated guide could force short covering on a stock 70% below its high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only up print, Q1 2026 at +13.7%, was a reiteration into a beaten-down stock, the same setup a squeeze would need.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the squeeze is conditional on the guide holding. The skew prices the downside path, not this one. If the market had priced a squeeze, the put skew would be flatter.
findings.independence: Baseline put/call OI ratio 0.29 and skew +14.58, from a different source (Yahoo options). Massive.com reported 31.19M short and 3.7 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement: https://massive.com/quote/stub.

findings.why_not_priced: The risk is widely known and the lockout itself would come after the window. Only call commentary can land inside it, and the company has not guided 2027 on a Q3 call before; it delayed its 2026 guide to March.

baseline_tension: The findings lean the same way as the +14.6 put skew and the -7% five-day slide (a flat peer secondary market, a stretched H2 EBITDA guide), so the downside view is largely what the market already holds. The positives (Citi's download read, the refinancing, moderate short interest) are the part that cuts against the skew, and p_up is held at 46 rather than lower for that reason.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (lands inside the guide; bar disputed): the peer flat-secondary finding lands inside the company's low single-digit H2 GMS guide and the aggregator revenue bar disagrees with BofA's estimate, so -1.0 became -0.6 and every finding stays capped small

Lesson 3 (two findings that cannot both be true): the EBITDA-stretch finding and Citi's 'high end reachable' view argue opposite sides of the FY guide. Kept as separate lines (guidance vs reported quarter) and the stretch was netted against Citi: -1.5 became -1.0
Lesson 1 (this name sells beats): Citi's Q3 EBITDA beat thesis lands on the reported quarter, and Q2's 94% EBITDA growth fell 10%, so +1.0 became +0.7
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the credit amendment buys a maturity extension at a tighter spread with no new money, so it stays a small positive (+0.3, unchanged)

Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was looked up (6.5 days to cover, ~7.7% of shares outstanding); not crowded enough to shrink the negatives further, so +0.5 is unchanged; the negatives agree with the skew
Outside the window: the MLB lockout event moved to outside_window; only call commentary stays as a finding, -0.3 to -0.2
